title: `isError`
description: The in-band flag marking a tool result as a tool execution error, which the spec expects clients to pass to the model so it can correct itself.
question: Can the agent tell a tool execution error from a successful result?
notes: Not one of the five hands the agent the boolean the specification defines. Three return the failure as ordinary text, so an agent reading the result cannot tell a failed call from a successful one. Two convert it into an exception, which preserves the fact of failure but moves it out of the result and into control flow.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: the failed call returns its text like any other result. Nothing marks it as a failure.
notes_by_num.2: LangChain: the error text arrives as an ordinary text block with a generated lc_ id. The flag is gone.
notes_by_num.3: OpenAI Agents: the error text is returned as normal tool output, indistinguishable from success.
notes_by_num.4: Pydantic AI: converted into a raised ModelRetry rather than a flag on the result. The failure is reachable, but as control flow.
notes_by_num.5: Mastra: converted into a thrown error rather than a flag on the result.

verdict.headline: Delivered by none of the five; two convert it into an exception.
verdict.detail: isError is how a tool says 'this did not work' without the agent having to read prose. Three frameworks erase that distinction entirely.

usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: MCP separates protocol errors from tool execution errors precisely so a model can retry the second kind with better arguments. A framework that raises both as exceptions, or reports both as success, collapses that distinction and removes the recovery path the spec designed.
